findings.body: At 80 columns, the strip uses the full layout because the compact layout starts below 80. The existing fixture's item line is already 91 characters, with `total` starting at character 84. Applying `truncate-end` to the whole line therefore hides the total and part of the round; longer titles also hide stages. This affects both surfaces. Reserve space for the required status and timing fields, shortening the title or adapting the layout before truncation.
findings.title: Not done: summary strip shows each stage's time and the total

findings.body: This cancels the repaint timer for every `session.end`, including `/clear`, `/resume` and `/branch`. Claude's documented lifecycle fires `session.start` only at module load or reload, so those actions never recreate the timer. Elapsed times consequently stop advancing between CORE's ten-second refreshes. Preserve the timer when the process continues, or restart it through an appropriate lifecycle event. See the [session event contract](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/mods/reference).
findings.title: Keep timer redraws active after clearing or resuming a session

findings.body: The new mounted pane and strip tests are not executed by the configured repository suite. `forge.toml:6` and `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:58` run pytest, while `tests/test_mod_plugin.py:54` only type-checks these native tests. Their assertions can therefore break without failing the supplied close run. `plans/FORGE-MOD-1.md:284` assigns the native plugin test job to SHIP, so this is deferred advice: that task must execute `claude plugin test` and propagate failures.
findings.title: Later: SHIP must run the native pane tests in the repository suite
